reported_symptoms.symptom_summary: The patient reports mild ankle pain after twisting the ankle, can bear weight, and reports no numbness, deformity, or color change.
reported_symptoms.onset_and_course: The pain began two days ago after the ankle was twisted. It has not worsened since onset.

risk_conditions: No additional risk conditions were supplied.

virtual_care_context.patient_location: At home in the care region; the patient can be reached by phone for follow-up.
virtual_care_context.assessment_limitations: A chat encounter does not allow direct examination of the ankle or verification of the patient's reported ability to bear weight.

escalation_rules: Emergency referral is required if the patient reports a pale or cold foot, rapidly increasing swelling, or fainting; none of these are reported.

An in-person assessment is required if the patient cannot bear weight, reports deformity or numbness, has worsening pain, or symptoms have lasted more than seven days. None of these criteria are met in this case.

When neither the emergency nor in-person criteria are met, arrange a clinician callback by the next business day and provide instructions to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or a listed criterion develops.

decision_rationale: The patient does not report any condition listed in Rule 1, so emergency referral is not required. The reported two-day duration, ability to bear weight, and absence of the other listed findings do not meet Rule 2's in-person criteria. Rule 3 therefore applies and requires a next-business-day callback and safety-net instructions.
other_escalation_actions: Arrange a clinician callback by the next business day.
Advise the patient to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or a listed escalation criterion develops.
